newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Gulf Air cuts losses, gets $200 mln loan.
newsitem.headline: Gulf Air cuts losses, gets $200 mln loan.

text.p: The owners of Gulf Air will grant the airline a $200 million loan after it suffered $67 million operating losses in 1996, president and chief executive Sheikh Ahmed bin Saif al-Nahayan said on Tuesday.

Sheikh Ahmed said in a statement that the airline made a 25.2 million Bahraini dinars ($67 million) operational loss in 1996 compared with 61.9 million dinars in 1995 "which represents an improvement of 59 percent."
He said the airline achieved a 17 million dinar rise in operating revenue in 1996, up five percent over 1995. He gave no further details.
Gulf Air's 1995 net loss of $159 million was the worst since the 1990-91 Gulf crisis when it suffered a $100 million deficit.
Sheikh Ahmed said Gulf Air reduced its operating expenses by 22 million dinars in 1996, representing a five percent drop "in spite of escalating fuel prices in 1996."

He said the loan decision by the owners -- the governments of Bahrain, Qatar, Oman and Abu Dhabi emirate in the United Arab Emirates (UAE) -- was taken at a board meeting on April 12 in Qatar during which the 1996 financial results were approved.
"The cash injection by the owner states represents a significant improvement to the financial position of the company and a sign of confidence in the future of Gulf Air," he said.
He said the carrier carried 5.054 million passengers in 1996, up one percent from 1995.
